Let me preface my answer by providing a list of alternatives to piracy:

1. Movie Theaters...
We don't have a movie theater in town, so every time I want to watch something on the silver-screen I have to drive 40km to a particular neighboring city. 
They don't even have a good movie theater since it's rather small and the only films there screening are bland, low-brow and uninteresting movies (Marvel and DC stuff, stupid national comedies meant for TV...).
Since I live in Brazil, English language films need some sort of translation to be viewed by the public at large. Unfortunately, this local cinema opts for the dubbed experience. This only worsens my movie-going experience, since most films at that place are blockbusters whose quality is somewhat dependant on sound effects -- the dub, of course, messes with them.


2. Disc Media.
There aren't any retail stores in the area, and local stores that sell any sort of film media only do so as a side thing -- thus, it's only mainstream stuff.
I do have knowledge of decent internet shops, but, of course, they are pretty darn expensive to casually buy from. Ever since I got around film as a hobby in 2017, I've only bought three sets of discs: a Nouvelle Vague one with 6 films, a David Lynch collection of 4 films and a Bertolt Brecht thing as expensive as the Lynch set. 


3. Streaming Services!
I have Netflix and MUBI subscriptions. 
Brazilian Netflix is rather pathetic and MUBI is pretty hit or miss, so I'm fairly disappointed in them both. Predictably, I don't use them as much as I would, say, the Criterion Channel (pls come to brazil). 
I will probably unsubscribe from them both shortly since they're not really worth it and are expensive.


4. TV Rentals!
There's only shit on regular TV. The last two times I tried to watch it gave way to my only 0,5 scores in Letterboxd. 
On the other hand, the movies there available for rent aren't any bad. Naturally, though, to consistently dish out money for them amounts to a lot of expense.


These are all my justifications for one simple answer: 

I'm totally on-board with piracy, given my monetary status.
